mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 12-month average precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate tighter credit conditions.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, no significant negative returns (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses above its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS relative to INDPRO indicates strengthening labor market demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 20% of such labor strength episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) below the 5-period moving average predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as it signals demand softening.
failure_condition: During demand contractions, 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (average p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls by more than 2% from its prior month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be negative due to supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, 5-day forward returns are not negative (mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% suggests central bank patience, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 40 such low-inflation periods, 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 shows a higher likelihood of positive 60-day forward returns as lower unemployment is expected.
failure_condition: In 30 such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (demand) and PAYEMS (employment) above their respective 10-period averages predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In 50 such dual-strength episodes, 20-day returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below the prior quarter's level combined with a decline in HOUST signals weak demand-supply alignment, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During 20 such events, 60-day returns are not persistently negative (average p-value > 0.15).
